6: # NuttX Driver Development
7: 
8: Follow the full driver lifecycle in order. Keep edits small and testable.
9: 
10: > [!TIP] This skill can be used standalone or via the `driver-workflow` agent (`agents/driver-workflow.agent.md`) for end-to-end driver development with automated reference matching, requirements generation, and PR submission.
11: 
12: ## Table of Contents
13: 
14: 1. [Preparation](#preparation)

16:    - Find reference drivers
17:    - Determine driver pattern
18:    - Layout driver files
19: 2. [Implementation](#implementation)

24: 3. [NuttX Coding & Kernel API Rules](#nuttx-coding--kernel-api-rules)

28: ---
29: 
30: ## Preparation
31: 
32: ### 1) Clarify scope and expectations
33: 
34: - Identify the NuttX driver subsystem (sensor, serial, timer, analog, etc.).
35: - Confirm target bus (I2C, SPI, 1-Wire, etc.) and required hardware properties.
36: - Clarify the NuttX source tree location. The driver code lives under `nuttx/drivers/`.
37: 
38: ### 2) Find reference drivers
39: 
40: > [!NOTE] Two types of reference drivers serve different purposes
41: >
42: > - **骨架参考（NuttX API 模式）**: 优先使用 NuttX in-tree 同类驱动作为代码骨架，确保符合 NuttX 的 upper-half/lower-half 架构和 VFS 集成方式
43: > - **芯片参考（寄存器/时序验证）**: 优先使用 Linux/Zephyr 同芯片驱动，用于交叉验证 datasheet 的寄存器定义、初始化序列、SPI 帧格式等芯片专属知识
44: >
45: > When used standalone: 手动搜索两类参考驱动
46: > When used with `driver-workflow` agent: Step A.2 自动完成两条线的并行搜索
47: 
48: Always look at the in-tree NuttX drivers before doing any work. There might already be a driver that (best scenario at the top):
49: 
50: 1. Is exactly the same part as the one you are working on
51: 2. Targets a very similar part from the same vendor (e.g., BMP280 vs BME680)
52: 3. Is the same device subsystem as yours (e.g., another I2C sensor)
53: 
54: If a reference driver is found, use it as a **skeleton template**:
55: 
56: 1. Copy the source file structure (function signatures, bus access pattern, registration flow, file layout)
57: 2. Replace all device-specific content: register definitions, chip ID values, vendor/chip names, init sequences, calibration logic
58: 3. After generating code, grep for the original chip name — zero matches required
59: 4. **Do NOT copy register addresses or chip-specific constants** — these must come from the target device's datasheet
60: 
61: Re-use these files/folders whenever possible:
62: - Header files in `include/nuttx/sensors/`, `include/nuttx/i2c/`, etc.
63: - Existing board-level registration patterns in `boards/`
64: 
65: If no suitable reference driver exists:
66: 
67: 1. Use the dispatch table below to load the subsystem-specific pattern reference
68: 2. Use the most similar subsystem's reference driver as template (e.g., use accelerometer driver as template for gyro)
69: 3. Follow the architectural pattern (uORB vs chardev) strictly from the loaded reference
70: 4. For 🔲 Planned subsystems, use `chardev_pattern.md` (Production-Quality Skeleton section) as the starting point
71: 
72: Here are the relevant folders to search for examples:
73: 
74: ```
75: nuttx/
76: ├── drivers/          # Device-specific driver sources. Search here first
77: │   ├── sensors/      # Sensor drivers (I2C/SPI/1-Wire)
78: │   ├── serial/       # UART/serial drivers
79: │   ├── i2c/          # I2C bus framework
80: │   ├── spi/          # SPI bus framework
81: │   ├── timers/       # Timer/watchdog/RTC drivers
82: │   ├── analog/       # ADC/DAC drivers
83: │   ├── leds/         # LED drivers
84: │   ├── input/        # Input device drivers
85: │   └── ...           # Many more subsystems
86: ├── include/nuttx/    # Public header files for driver APIs
87: │   ├── sensors/      # Sensor driver headers & sensor_lowerhalf_s
88: │   ├── i2c/          # I2C master interface (i2c_master_s)
89: │   ├── spi/          # SPI interface (spi_dev_s)
90: │   └── fs/           # VFS file_operations, register_driver()
91: ├── boards/           # Board-specific initialization & driver registration
92: └── arch/             # Architecture-specific lower-half bus implementations
93: ```
94: 
95: Use `references/nuttx_nav_search.md` for driver examples and navigating the NuttX repo.
96:

152: #### Pattern A: Upper-Half / Lower-Half — Preferred for Subsystem Drivers
153: 
154: Most NuttX driver subsystems (sensors, timers, serial, audio, etc.) use an upper-half/lower-half split. The upper-half provides the VFS interface and common logic; you only implement the lower-half callbacks.
155: 
156: ```
157: Application
158:     │  open/read/write/ioctl/poll
159:     ▼
160:   VFS (/dev/...)
161:     │
162:     ▼
163:   Upper-half (provided by NuttX)  ← Generic, handles VFS + common logic
164:     │  subsystem-specific callbacks
165:     ▼
166:   Lower-half (your driver)  ← You implement these
167:     │
168:     ▼
169:   Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_*)
170: ```
171: 
172: **When to use**: Always prefer this when the subsystem provides an upper-half framework. Load the corresponding reference document from the dispatch table for implementation details.
173: 
174: #### Pattern B: Standalone Character Device Driver
175: 
176: The simplest pattern. The driver directly implements `struct file_operations` and registers with `register_driver()`.
177: 
178: ```
179: Application
180:     │  open/read/write/ioctl/close
181:     ▼
182:   VFS (/dev/mydevN)
183:     │
184:     ▼
185:   file_operations  ← Your driver implements these
186:     │
187:     ▼
188:   Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_LOCK+SPI_SELECT+SPI_RECVBLOCK)
189: ```
190: 
191: **When to use**: Only when the device doesn't fit any existing subsystem, or when existing in-tree drivers for the same device class already use this pattern (e.g., some vibrator or custom peripheral drivers).
192: 
193: See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for standalone character device implementation details.
194: 
195: ### 4) Layout the driver files
196: 
197: Define the files that will be created/modified. The exact layout depends on the subsystem — refer to the loaded reference document for subsystem-specific examples.
198: 
199: General layout:
200: 
201: ```
202: nuttx/
203: ├── drivers/<subsystem>/
204: │   ├── mydevice.c            # Driver implementation
205: │   ├── Make.defs             # Add CSRCS += mydevice.c
206: │   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Add list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
207: │   └── Kconfig               # Add CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE entry
208: ├── include/nuttx/<subsystem>/
209: │   └── mydevice.h            # Public header: register function prototype
210: └── boards/<arch>/<chip>/<board>/src/
211:     └── <board>_mydevice.c    # Board-level init: get bus, call register
212: ```
213: 
214: ## Implementation
215: 
216: > [!info] TLDR
217: >
218: > - Implement C driver (lower-half callbacks OR file_operations)
219: > - Create public header file with register function prototype
220: > - Add Kconfig entry for driver enable/disable
221: > - Add source to Make.defs and CMakeLists.txt
222: > - Write board-level registration code
223: 
224: ### Write the Driver C Implementation
225: 
226: For subsystem-specific implementation (sensor uORB, timer, LED, etc.), load the corresponding reference document from the Driver Type Dispatch Table above.
227: 
228: The following sections cover **cross-subsystem generic patterns** that apply to all driver types.
229: 
230: #### Bus Access (I2C / SPI)
231: 
232: For I2C/SPI register read/write helpers, bulk transfer patterns, SPI frame protocols (8-bit and 16-bit), and SPI mode detection — read `references/bus_access.md` when writing bus access code.
233: 
234: ### Write the Public Header File
235: 
236: Create `include/nuttx/<subsystem>/mydevice.h`. The header content depends on the driver pattern:
237: 
238: - **Upper-half/lower-half drivers**: Header contains only the register function prototype
239: - **Standalone char device drivers**: Header also defines data structures for `read()`
240: 
241: See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for char device header examples.
242: 
243: ### Kconfig
244: 
245: Add your driver entry to the appropriate `Kconfig` file (e.g., `drivers/<subsystem>/Kconfig`):
246: 
247: ```kconfig
248: config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE
249: 	bool "MyVendor MYDEVICE sensor/device support"
250: 	default n
251: 	---help---
252: 		Enable driver for the MyVendor MYDEVICE.
253: 
254: if <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE
255: 
256: choice
257: 	prompt "MYDEVICE Interface"
258: 	default <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_SPI
259: 
260: config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_I2C
261: 	bool "MYDEVICE I2C Interface"
262: 	select I2C
263: 	---help---
264: 		Enables support for the I2C interface
265: 
266: config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_SPI
267: 	bool "MYDEVICE SPI Interface"
268: 	select SPI
269: 	---help---
270: 		Enables support for the SPI interface
271: 
272: endchoice
273: 
274: endif # <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE
275: ```
276: 
277: Key Kconfig conventions:
278: - Use `select I2C` or `select SPI` to auto-enable bus dependency
279: - Use `depends on` for soft dependencies
280: - Group device-specific options inside `if ... endif`
281: - Provide `---help---` text for every user-visible option
282: - For devices supporting both I2C and SPI, use a `choice` block
283: - Default interface should match the most common usage (check reference designs)
284: 
285: ### Make.defs
286: 
287: Add your source file to `drivers/<subsystem>/Make.defs`:
288: 
289: ```makefile
290: ifeq ($(CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE),y)
291:   CSRCS += mydevice.c
292: endif
293: ```
294: 
295: > [!NOTE] File naming convention
296: >
297: > - Upper-half/lower-half drivers with framework: `mydevice_uorb.c` (sensors), `mydevice.c` (others)
298: > - Standalone char device drivers: `mydevice.c`
299: > - Check existing in-tree drivers for the naming convention used in your subsystem.
300: > - The Make.defs entry does NOT need to be under an `ifeq ($(CONFIG_I2C),y)` guard
301: >   if the Kconfig already uses `select I2C` — the bus will always be enabled.
302: 
303: The Make.defs file **must** end with the DEPPATH/VPATH/CFLAGS block (already present in existing files).
304: 
305: ### CMakeLists.txt
306: 
307: Add your source file to `drivers/<subsystem>/CMakeLists.txt`:
308: 
309: ```cmake
310: if(CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE)
311:   list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
312: endif()
313: ```
314: 
315: ### Board-Level Registration
316: 
317: See `references/board_registration.md` for complete board-level registration patterns for both upper-half/lower-half and standalone char device drivers.
318: 
319: ## NuttX Coding & Kernel API Rules
320: 
321: For all coding style rules, kernel API usage, initialization timing, work queue selection, interrupt patterns, synchronization primitives, RPMsg rules, and error cleanup patterns — read `references/coding_rules.md` when writing or reviewing driver code.
322: 
323: Quick reference (always run after generating code):
324: 
325: ```bash
326: nuttx/tools/checkpatch.sh -f <your_file.c>
327: ```
328: 
329: ## Code Review
330: 
331: 6-dimension review covering initialization, power management, API usage,
332: critical section & ISR, runtime environment, and coding style.
333: 
334: ### Review Process
335: 
336: 1. Read `.c`, `.h`, Kconfig, Make.defs, CMakeLists.txt. Identify driver pattern
337:    (uORB sensor / standalone chardev / RPMsg / other upper-half/lower-half).
338: 2. Run 6-dimension checklist — mark each item PASS / WARN / FAIL.
339:    See [driver_review_checklist.md](references/driver_review_checklist.md).
340: 3. Run nxstyle check: `nuttx/tools/checkpatch.sh -f <file.c>` (skip if unavailable).
341: 4. Generate structured report (template in checklist reference).
342: 5. For each FAIL/WARN: provide line number + fix snippet + rule reference.
343: 
344: ### Review Rules
345: 
346: - FAIL items must be fixed before submission. Auto-fix and re-check until zero FAIL.
347: - WARN items are listed for user decision.
348: - If more than 5 issues found on file save, recommend running full review.

5: 
6: # openvela Build
7: 
8: 编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。
9: 
10: ## 默认目标
11: 
12: 默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：
13: 
14: ```
15: CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
16: OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
17: ```
18: 
19: 如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。
20: 
21: ## 命令
22: 
23: ### 编译
24: 
25: ```bash
26: ./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
27: ```
28: 
29: 示例：
30: ```bash
31: ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
32: ```
33: 
34: **成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`
35: 
36: **编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`
37: 
38: ### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）
39: 
40: ```bash
41: ./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
42: ```
43: 
44: menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。
45: 
46: 修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
47: ```bash
48: ./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
49: ```
50: 
51: ### 运行模拟器
52: 
53: ```bash
54: ./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
55: ```
56: 
57: 示例：
58: ```bash
59: ./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
60: ```
61: 
62: **成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符
63: 
64: ### 清理编译
65: 
66: ```bash
67: rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>
68: ```
69: 
70: 全量清理后重新编译：
71: ```bash
72: rm -rf cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ && ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
73: ```
74: 
75: ## 编译流程
76: 
77: 1. 用户指定或确认目标配置路径
78: 2. 执行 `./build.sh <path> --cmake -j$(nproc)`
79: 3. 检查输出最后几行是否包含 `build completed successfully`
80: 4. 如果编译失败，分析错误日志并尝试修复（最多 3 轮）
81: 
82: ## 编译失败处理
83: 
84: | 错误类型 | 特征 | 处理 |
85: |----------|------|------|
86: | 代码错误 | `error:` + 本驱动文件名 | 自动修复代码，重新编译 |
87: | 配置缺失 | `undefined reference` + CONFIG 相关 | 提示用户 menuconfig 开启 |
88: | 工具链问题 | `command not found` | 提示用户安装工具链 |
89: | 缓存问题 | 奇怪的链接错误 | `rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>` 后重编 |
90: 
91: ## 启用新驱动的 CONFIG
92: 
93: 如果需要临时启用某个 CONFIG 进行编译验证：
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # 方法 1: 直接追加到 defconfig（推荐）
97: echo "CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y" >> <CONFIG_PATH>/defconfig
98: 
99: # 方法 2: 用 sed 修改 .config（临时，不持久化）
100: sed -i 's/# CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680 is not set/CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y/' <OUTPUT_DIR>/.config
101: ```
102: 
103: 修改后重新编译即可。
104: 
105: ## 常用配置路径
106: 
107: | 目标 | 配置路径 |
108: |------|----------|
109: | goldfish-arm64 (推荐) | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/` |
110: | goldfish-arm32 | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap/` |
111: | 自定义板级 | `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/configs/<config>/` |
